answer: One concrete defense is slashable stake weighting: an agent earns influence by locking capital, and voting power tracks the locked amount, not the count of identities. Splitting one wallet into a garden of fake agents cannot multiply that power, since the same jade collateral is merely divided among them and any shard caught certifying a false result is slashed. To climb toward the summit of governance an attacker must lock real capital under every alias, so influence costs the same whether it comes from one name or a thousand, and a single detected lie burns the whole bond.
